notes:
**Windows** — run `ruze_0.0.36_x64-setup.exe`.
**Linux** — `flatpak install ruze-0.0.36.flatpak`, then `flatpak run com.ruze.chat`.
**Android** — sideload `ruze-0.0.36.apk`. arm64 devices, Android 8.0 or newer.

---

### Changed

- **Joining a server is quiet now.** The modem handshake that played over a
  join is gone. It was written to last exactly as long as the join took, and
  that turned out to have no upper bound: a join that never finished never
  stopped it. On Android that outlived the thing that started it — swiping the
  app away closed the window and left the handshake negotiating on its own,
  over a connection that never came up. The connection log it played over is
  unchanged, and it was the half doing the useful work: every line in it is a
  step the app actually reached.

- **A preference set in one window reaches the others straight away.** The
  theme, the accent, whether the app icon follows it, the notification sounds,
  animated emoji and link previews are all settings you change in the main
  window and see in every window. Until now the friends window and any
  popped-out conversation kept drawing the old one until they were closed and
  opened again — so turning off animated emoji left them animating in the very
  window you were reading.

### Fixed

- **Somebody on their phone is not somebody who is offline.** The dot beside a
  member only ever checked the one device a server happened to have written
  down for them, so a person signed in on a second device read as away when
  they were sitting in the channel. It now counts any device of theirs.

- **The app no longer says people are offline when it means it cannot tell.**
  Whether anyone is reachable is learned from the peers this device is
  connected to, and that set is empty for a moment after a server opens and
  for as long as nothing is connected. Every member was marked offline in the
  meantime, which reported this device's own silence as a fact about everyone
  else. When nothing is connected the list says so instead.

- **The count beside a server counts people, not connections.** It was counting
  network links, so one person signed in twice counted twice, and it read
  "1 online" — you — while nothing was connected at all. It now says "not
  connected" when that is what is true.

- **Leaving a server lets go of it.** Its members, channels, unread counts and
  icon stayed in memory for the rest of the session, so rejoining the same
  server before restarting drew the old list until fresh information arrived.

- **Unfriending somebody closes the door in every window.** A conversation
  opened in its own window went on listing them as a friend, because that
  window was never told. It is told now — and the app is arranged so the next
  window cannot be forgotten the same way.
